theme.title: Quiet Session
theme.summary: Consumer Staples (+0.29%) and Health Care (+0.13%) led the market today, while Consumer Discretionary (-0.28%) and Utilities (-0.12%) brought up the rear. Performance didn't cluster cleanly by style — growth averaged -0.05%, defensives +0.10%, and value/cyclicals -0.01% — more a stock-by-stock market than a single broad theme. Major indices moved in a tighter band — S&P 500 -0.06%, Dow -0.11%, Nasdaq -0.32% — without one clearly dominating. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at -0.56%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX rose 0.45% to 15.53, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold slipped 0.50% to $4,454.70, crude oil was little changed at $82.37, and bitcoin gained 0.57% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
